extracted.intended_audience: DoD/Navy managers, contract administrators, and researchers studying OMB Circular A-76/Commercial Activities implementation
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and empirical research on implementing the Commercial Activities (A-76) program in the Navy, including the four-phase cost-comparison process, PWS/PRS requirements, MEO development, cost-estimating rules, and post-award monitoring issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Four-phase CA program process
rubrics_metrics.description: The process involved in implementing the policy outlined in OMB Circular A-76 consists of basically four phases: inventory, management review, cost comparison, and implementation of the results of the cost comparison.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inventory identifies activities ashore that can be performed by commercial sources; management review examines special circumstances/exemptions; cost comparison determines whether government or contractor is more economical; implementation enacts the decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventory: identify commercial-eligible functions
rubrics_metrics.description: The inventory phase involves the identification of Navy activities ashore that can be performed by commercial sources. This includes all those functions that are not excluded because they are 'governmental in nature' as outlined previously.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Functions excluded as governmental in nature should not be inventoried as commercial activities; inventory is the first filter for potential cost comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Management review: identify exemptions/special circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: The management review phase involves systematic examination and analysis by the activity to identify any special circumstances that would preclude performance of the function by a commercial source.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPNAV (OP-443) examines each function to determine whether it should be retained in-house for national defense reasons. Valid national defense exemptions include mobilization and contingency requirements, military training requirements, maintaining the Navy's sea/shore rotation base and depot and intermediate level maintenance requirements. Other exemptions may be granted case-by-case for core logistics functions and patient care at DOD hospitals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision to conduct cost study (OPNAV review)
rubrics_metrics.description: The process is initiated when the local command submits a review format via the chain of command to OPNAV (OP-443) with certain data specified by OPNAVINST 4860.6C. The data are examined and a decision is made whether to conduct a cost study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow OPNAVINST 4860.6C data requirements; OPNAV determines if a full cost comparison study is warranted based on the review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance Work Statement (PWS) development
rubrics_metrics.description: The task analysis involved in the development of the PWS must identify and quantify the output generated by the function. The PWS forms the basis of both the government's and commercial sources' cost estimations/bids and therefore must accurately reflect what is desired in terms of quality and performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PWS should, 'insofar as possible, specify work only in terms of its outcome, rather than in terms of the procedures used to achieve that outcome.' Leave procedural matters to competing activities to allow maximum flexibility for efficiencies. Accurately quantifying outputs is one of the most difficult and critical tasks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of generic/standard PWSs
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognizing the importance of the PWS and to assist field activities, standard or generic PWSs for the various functional areas have been developed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Completed DOD generic PWSs for CA functional areas are collected by DLSIE (Fort Lee, VA) for dissemination upon request; use these to ensure consistency across studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance Requirements Summary (PRS) and Acceptable Quality Level (AQL)
rubrics_metrics.description: The PWS includes a Performance Requirements Summary (PRS) which stipulates the performance standards or quality levels that must be met. Included in the PRS, in addition to the Acceptable Quality Level (AQL), is a deduction percentage approximating the importance assigned to each performance measure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PRS levels represent allowable deviation from 'perfect' work before monetary assessments (deductions) are applied. Performance quality standards should be objectively measurable; PRS forms the basis of contractor Quality Control and government Quality Assurance programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality Assurance/Quality Control responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality control is part of the contractor's responsibility; the government's Quality Assurance program is implemented using government employees (Quality Assurance Evaluators or Contract Compliance Representatives) who conduct regular surveillance to ensure PWS compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While a formal QA program is not required for government performance, the MEO must provide capability for evaluating and documenting government performance to PWS standards. QAEs perform surveillance and can issue deductions or discrepancy reports for noncompliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Management study and Most Efficient Organization (MEO)
rubrics_metrics.description: The management study/review ensures the in-house workforce is organized and staffed as efficiently and effectively as possible and that internal procedures foster efficient production; once completed, the organization is restructured into the Most Efficient Organization (MEO).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Objective: optimize job structure and operating procedures within current resources before costing the MEO; the MEO is the government baseline bid for cost comparison.

rubrics_metrics.name: In-house cost estimate rules (Cost Comparison Handbook guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailed guidance for preparation of the in-house cost estimate is contained in the Cost Comparison Handbook; category and line-by-line computational techniques include guidance on inflation, personnel costs, materials and supplies, depreciation, overhead, contract administration, conversion costs, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a function is identified as a commercial activity, military positions shall be converted to civilian positions for cost comparison purposes; estimates are for an 'all civilian' operation; follow handbook rules closely to avoid contested computations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sealed bidding and comparison rule
rubrics_metrics.description: The MEO is costed out and presented to the Contracting Officer in a sealed bid. The government's bid is compared to that of the lowest, competent and responsive private bidder and a decision is made to either retain in-house (implement MEO) or contract out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use sealed bidding conventions; compare to lowest competent/responsive bidder; incorporate required labor differentials before making contracting decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: MEO labor differential and contractor bid components
rubrics_metrics.description: Contractor bids normally include an estimate of contract administration costs (normally 4-8% of the MEO bid) but exclude the 10% of MEO personnel costs that are added before making the actual contract-out decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before final decision, add the required 10% MEO labor cost differential; account for contract administration costs and other mandated adjustments so comparisons are on an equivalent basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of Service Contract Act wage determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Service Contract Act of 1965 provides for minimum wages, benefits and working conditions for service contract employees via Department of Labor wage rate determinations. The wage determination serves as a bottom limit for the contractor and can reduce contractor cost flexibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Absence or later establishment of a wage determination can materially change contract price (example: follow-on contract increased by 83.9% after wage determination was set); account for geographic wage determinants when estimating contractor costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-award transaction cost monitoring
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no formal accounting system that captures litigation costs, conversion costs, contract administration costs in excess of that allowed for in the cost comparison process, quality or substandard performance costs, or the cost of contingency operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize and attempt to capture post-award transaction costs that pre-award cost comparisons may ignore; lack of monitoring leads to debate and potential uncontrolled resource allocation issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transition and contingency guidance (default/bankruptcy)
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no formal guidance to commands on how to accomplish the 'contracted out' function in the event of contractor default or bankruptcy or how to manage resource/fund cuts when functions are performed commercially.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Planning for contractor failure, budget reductions, and 'back-up' government capability is critical—especially for umbrella contracts where many base support functions are outsourced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance evaluation methods and data needs
rubrics_metrics.description: Performance assessments were made primarily by using observation and Quality Assurance inspections; many also used external inspection results and customer satisfaction measures. Few commands provided pre-award vs post-award performance statistics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use multiple objective measures (observations, QA inspections, external inspections, customer satisfaction) and maintain pre/post award performance statistics to substantiate assessments and enable better monitoring and control systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of deductions and Contract Discrepancy Reports (CDRs)
rubrics_metrics.description: A majority (56%) of commands had taken deductions for substandard performance; some commands issued Contract Discrepancy Reports in addition to deductions. Deduction amounts reported were generally less than 1% of contract price.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure contracts include deduction clauses; use CDRs to document and support deductions; keep records of deductions and associated QA reports for accountability and potential litigation support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contractor experience and PWS modifications
rubrics_metrics.description: All respondents indicated current contractors were experienced; ~67% had performed similar work for Navy/DoD previously. ~67% indicated modifications were made to the PWS during the course of the contract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor experienced contractors when appropriate; expect and allow for PWS modifications over time; recognize that PWS inadequacies can lead to claims and settlements (example: prior settlement ~ $30K due to PWS inadequacies).

rubrics_metrics.name: Awareness of implicit assumptions and debate points
rubrics_metrics.description: The CA program implicitly assumes pre-award estimates accurately reflect all post-award costs. Debate centers on fairness, quality, accountability, potential deterioration in quality, loss of managerial control and flexibility, morale, and hidden costs not captured pre-award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critically evaluate pre-award assumptions; consider both proponents' claims (market strengthening, cost savings) and opponents' claims (quality and accountability problems). Identify root causes such as poorly written specifications and substandard quality surveillance and address them in PWS and QA design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical metrics for program assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Program statistics used include number of cost studies, positions involved, net total program savings, percentage of studies resulting in continued in-house operation vs conversion to contract, and cost differentials between MEO and contractor bids.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track and report these metrics (e.g., FY1979-FY1987: 823 studies, ~22,000 positions, net savings $495.2M; sample statistics such as average cost differential 17.66% for studied activities) to evaluate program performance and trends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research/sample selection criteria for CA studies
rubrics_metrics.description: To determine the population of CA cost comparisons, obtain the OPNAV-443 database listing sorted by 'Primary Function Studied' and select studies coded for functional areas of interest (e.g., S713 Food Service, T801 Storage and Warehousing) as primary or secondary function codes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform manual review to identify multifunction/umbrella contracts (one primary code plus secondary codes). For empirical studies, define geographic/time constraints (example: West Coast/Hawaii focus due to accessibility) and document exclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data gathering methodology standards for empirical CA research
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary data gathering methods included formal interview/written responses using a mailed questionnaire, and informal follow-up interviews (phone). Key personnel included Service Contract Managers (SCMs), Contracting Officer Technical Representatives (COTRs), Contracting Officers (KOs) and Comptrollers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use an interview questionnaire (example: included in Appendix B), assure anonymity, follow up for clarifications, supplement with literature review and audits, and corroborate with OPNAV statistical databases and Cost Comparison Handbook guidance.
